public_body: Nantucket Planning And Economic Development Commission
overall: The Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by omitting the nonunion employee's name from Purpose 2 notices and discussing matters outside Purpose 2; it must re-vote the contract in open session within 45 days or the May 22 approval is nullified.

allegations.summary: Commission argued the complaint was untimely because violations could have been discovered over 30 days before filing; the AG rejected that argument.
allegations.key_passage: As the complaint was filed on June 19, it was timely.

allegations.summary: Executive session notices for Purpose 2 did not name the nonunion employee (the deputy director) who was the subject of the discussions.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons, the notices should have referenced Ms. Snell in relation to the Purpose 2 executive session.

allegations.summary: Executive session discussed the director's retirement announcement and the deputy's qualifications for the post, which allegedly fell outside Purpose 2.
allegations.key_passage: Here, discussions of matters outside the narrow scope of Purpose 2, including the Director’s announcement of his retirement and a discussion in the Deputy Director’s presence of her qualifications to take his place, ran afoul of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A contract for the new director was approved in executive session on March 20 and the successor appointment was effectively settled behind closed doors before the May 22 open-session announcement.
allegations.key_passage: The vote to execute an agreed-upon contract must take place in open session.

remedy: Post adequate notice and, in open session, discuss the hiring of a Director of Planning and vote to approve the resulting contract within 45 days; if not, the May 22 approval is nullified.

Release to the public the minutes of the February 23 and March 20 executive sessions as they relate to the topics addressed, along with documents used in that portion of the session, such as the contract.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: Additionally, we order the Commission to release to the public minutes of the executive sessions held on February 23 and March 20 as they relate to the topics addressed herein and any documents used during that portion of the executive session, such as the contract.
